title: Retrieval practice produces more learning than elaborative studying with concept mapping.

sources.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating the replicability of social science experiments in Nature and Science between 2010 and 2015
sources.finding: The preregistered independent replication reports positive significant focal results for both Aviezer and Karpicke/Blunt in Figure 1. Original-author reviewed protocols; not every original experiment was repeated.

sources.title: Ritchie, Della Sala and McIntosh: Retrieval Practice, with or without Mind Mapping, Boosts Fact Learning in Primary School Children
sources.finding: Independent in-class experiments adapted the retrieval/mapping comparison to 8–12-year-olds and geographical facts. Retrieval benefited recall through five weeks; mind mapping gave no consistent benefit. This simpler mapping task is not identical to original adult concept mapping.

sources.title: Mayrhofer, Kuhbandner and Frischholz: Re-examining the testing effect as a learning strategy
sources.finding: Preregistered N=230 comparison reproduces original verbatim recall advantage under original conditions. Adding memorization to concept mapping removes that advantage; inference performance does not favor retrieval. Single German text, one-week retention; authors acknowledge these boundaries.

sources.title: American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation: Study Tips & Resources
sources.finding: Official professional-exam guidance recommends self-testing and cites this paper among research supporting the advice. Demonstrates adoption into guidance, not measured candidate compliance or attribution of the whole testing-effect literature to this paper.

summary: The original comparison reproduced and stimulated independent classroom and methodological work. A preregistered 2023 study challenges attributing the advantage specifically to retrieval, because extra memorization removes the gap. This mixed outcome is not a blanket failure or universal validation.
researcher: Codex independent blind repeat by expand_manylabs; first grade not viewed
central_claims: Retrieval practice improves conceptual learning more than elaborative concept mapping.
The advantage reflects retrieval-specific mechanisms rather than elaboration alone.
